frames.observation: The exact Cinderwing body is readable in settled batFlySlow at 58 HP. The dark head and torso, pale muzzle, red-orange wing membranes, feet and tail form one compact airborne silhouette.
A later batFlySlow upstroke keeps both segmented wings attached and balanced around the body without sampled inversion or vertex burst.
At the pinned AttackProf trigger boundary the bat remains centered and recognizable through camera blur and the bright ground effect.
During batAttackProf the body pitches and the wings fold coherently. Radiance obscures the underside, but no authored section appears detached.
The bat has returned to batFlySlow after AttackProf. Its face and both wings remain visible above the lingering radial effect.
At the start of attackCrit_bat the exact model advances with the long wing silhouette intact and the head still aligned between the wings.
The attackCrit_bat lunge overlaps the foreground hero and bright impact effect. Visible red wing sections remain joined to the dark body, while the occlusion limits fine deformation review.
The model is back in batFlySlow after attackCrit_bat with its face, torso and both wings readable at normal combat distance.
The ordinary no-focus player attack begins from a settled 58 HP batFlySlow pose with the exact body fully visible.
At the pinned native damage-action frame the bat remains in its coherent flight pose before the later Damaged trigger.

At the native Damaged trigger the foreground hero and impact sphere cover most of the bat. The HP surface has begun resolving from 58 toward the measured 48 endpoint, so this frame proves timing but limits visual inspection.
During batTakeHit the bat is partly hidden behind the hero, but a folded red wing and aligned body remain visible while the ordinary 10-damage label resolves.
The first recovery frame returns to batFlySlow at 48 HP. Hero overlap still hides part of the model, while the visible wing remains coherent.
A later native attackCrit_bat begins from the recovered 48 HP flight pose with both wings attached and the face readable.
The critical lunge reaches the hero with the bat body and near wing still joined. The large Steadfast shield effect limits the far wing and contact view.
The bat has recovered to its normal airborne silhouette after the second native attack; lingering Steadfast effects remain in the foreground.
The separate explicit KillSingle fixture begins from a settled coherent batFlySlow pose at 48 HP.
At the pinned native Death trigger the impact sphere and hero hide most of the bat. This exact frame establishes trigger timing but is not used for a fine deformation claim.
The first retained batDeath frame shows the body entering its fall amid native red particles. Visible wing sections remain connected to the central body.
During batDeath the model descends behind the hero with red native particles around it. No visible authored section has exploded or inverted.
The animated death has placed the bat on the floor with its head, body and spread wings still forming a coherent visible shape.
The same floor pose remains visible behind the Victory loot overlay at the final sampled frame. Depth blur and the panel limit detail, and no lifetime beyond this capture is claimed.

requirements: All 22 referenced original PNGs were inspected at original resolution before assigning this reviewed status.
The ordinary no-focus gameplay claim is limited to the same-target HP change from 58 to 48; the separate KillSingle fixture is not ordinary lethal evidence.
The death claim is an animated batDeath path with m_DoRagdoll=false and zero rigid bodies, not a ragdoll claim.
The exact renderer remained active, enabled and visible in all 360 retained frames; selected originals support visual conclusions only for their sampled views.
Native UI, attack effects, foreground hero overlap, loot overlay, depth blur and camera movement limit fine surface, culling and corpse inspection.
